scope: Named cold-hardy grape cultivars for fresh eating, juice, jelly and wine, shippable to Annandale, NJ (zone 6b/7a): American (Vitis labrusca and relatives) and cold-hardy American-European hybrids that survive zone 5-6 winters. Muscadines (zone 7b+), ungrafted European wine grapes (V. vinifera) and unnamed generic vines are left out. Own-rooted vines are the norm here; grafted vines are noted.

varieties.name: Concord
varieties.summary: Classic blue-black American slipskin grape for juice, jelly and fresh eating.
varieties.description: Medium clusters of large blue-black, tough-skinned berries with a strong labrusca flavor, used for jelly, juice, wine and fresh eating. Ripens mid to late season (about 2-3 weeks after Bluebell at Fedco). Self-fertile; Fedco rates it hardy to about -17F (zone 5) and suggests Bluebell for colder sites; Edible Landscaping notes strong disease resistance.

varieties.name: Concord Seedless
varieties.summary: Seedless sport of Concord with the same blue-black color and labrusca flavor.
varieties.description: Blue-black slipskin berries with Concord character, typically used for jelly and juice, with slightly smaller clusters and berries than Concord and earlier maturity. Ripens late August through September. Double A lists zones 4-8 and notes susceptibility to black rot; Roots to Fruits and Willis list zones 5-8 and 5-9.

varieties.name: Niagara
varieties.summary: The standard green (white) labrusca grape, for juice, table and sweet wine.
varieties.description: Large clusters of amber-green slipskin berries with a strong foxy labrusca flavor, used for fresh eating, white juice and sweet wine. Very productive and vigorous; Edible Landscaping notes fair disease resistance with occasional black rot spraying. Zone range quoted varies by seller (3-7 to 5-9).

varieties.name: Catawba
varieties.summary: Heritage pink-red labrusca grape with a spicy flavor, used for juice, jelly and sparkling wine.
varieties.description: Early-1800s American chance seedling with thick-skinned, slipskin, aromatic pink to purplish-red berries in medium-large clusters. Good fresh, for juice, jelly and sparkling wine; ripens late September to October. Fedco rates it zone 5 and says it may need less spraying than its old reputation suggests.

varieties.name: Bluebell
varieties.summary: Very cold-hardy, Concord-like blue grape that ripens 2-3 weeks before Concord.
varieties.description: Medium dark berries with a blue bloom, thick skin and mild Concord-like flavor for fresh eating, juice and preserves. Ripens about 2-3 weeks ahead of Concord and tolerates about -30F with good resistance to fungal disease at Fedco. Seeded.

varieties.name: Himrod
varieties.summary: Early, very sweet seedless green-gold table grape with a honey-like flavor.
varieties.description: Pale golden seedless berries with tender skin and juicy, honey-like sweetness in large loose clusters; ripens early to mid-September. Good for fresh eating, juice and raisins. Seller zone ratings vary (5-9 at Roots to Fruits, 6-8 at One Green World).

varieties.name: Reliance
varieties.summary: Hardy seedless pink-red table grape with a strawberry-like flavor.
varieties.description: Large, loose clusters of tender, melting pinkish-red berries with a strawberry-like labrusca flavor, very early ripening; good fresh, for juice and jelly, and stores 1-2 months in a root cellar per Fedco. Hardy to about -25F (zone 4) per Roots to Fruits and Fedco; Fedco notes vines have stayed disease-free for them though literature warns of susceptibility.

breeder.name: University of Arkansas grape breeding program (1982)

varieties.name: Canadice
varieties.summary: Early seedless red table grape with a subtle spice note.
varieties.description: Compact clusters of medium pink to light red seedless berries with tender, edible slipskin and a distinct labrusca flavor with a hint of spice. Ripens about two weeks ahead of Concord in late summer and holds well on the vine. Self-fertile; sellers rate it hardy to roughly -10F (zones 6-8 at One Green World, 3-8 at Nature Hills).

varieties.name: Mars
varieties.summary: Very early, disease-resistant blue seedless grape with Concord-type flavor.
varieties.description: Large seedless blue berries with a musky Concord-like flavor and thick slipskin that resists cracking, good for fresh eating, juice and jelly. Very early ripening (mid-August in central Maine) and rated among the best for disease resistance at Fedco. Vigorous; Fedco rates it zone 5 (trial in zone 4) after exposure to -20F.

breeder.name: University of Arkansas grape breeding program (1984)

varieties.name: Jupiter
varieties.summary: Large seedless blue grape with a mild muscat flavor and crisp flesh.
varieties.description: Large clusters of large reddish-blue to dark blue, non-slipskin berries with a mild muscat flavor, crunchy texture and thin, crack-resistant skin; ripens mid-August and holds on the vine. Self-fertile; One Green World rates it zones 6-9, hardy to at least -10F.

breeder.name: University of Arkansas grape breeding program

varieties.name: Venus
varieties.summary: Early seedless blue-black grape with sweet, slightly muscat flavor.
varieties.description: Large blue-black seedless berries in tight, full clusters that ripen together, with a sweet fruity flavor and a hint of muscat. Early (August) and crack-resistant, very vigorous and productive; stores well. Zone ratings vary by seller (4-9 at One Green World, 6-10 at Willis).

breeder.name: University of Arkansas grape breeding program

varieties.name: Einset Seedless
varieties.summary: Seedless red slipskin table grape with a strawberry-like labrusca flavor.
varieties.description: Medium clusters of oval bright red seedless berries with tender, edible slipskin and a distinct labrusca-strawberry flavor; the soft seed remnant is not noticeable. Ripens early. Hardiness is not stated by the sellers read here.

varieties.name: Vanessa
varieties.summary: Crisp, deep red seedless table grape with a fine, mildly fruity flavor.
varieties.description: Medium clusters of firm, crisp, deep-red seedless berries with a sweet, fruity non-labrusca flavor, also usable for raisins. Mid-season and vigorous; Fedco rates it zone 4 and reports it re-sprouting from the base after dieback at -20F.

breeder.name: K.H. Fisher and O.A. Bradt, Vineland Station, Ontario (1983)

varieties.name: Somerset Seedless
varieties.summary: Early, cold-hardy seedless grape with crisp strawberry-flavored red fruit.
varieties.description: Medium loose clusters of small to medium sweet reddish-golden berries with a crisp texture and strawberry-like flavor, ripening early (August). Not overly vigorous and easy to grow; Fedco rates it hardy to about -30F (zone 4).

varieties.name: Marquis
varieties.summary: Large, sweet pale-yellow seedless grape, disease resistant.
varieties.description: Abundant crops of large, pale yellow, very sweet and flavorful seedless berries with a melting texture that hold well on the vine. Ripens mid-September; One Green World lists it as disease resistant, zones 6-9, hardy to -10F.

varieties.name: Neptune
varieties.summary: Large-clustered seedless green grape with fruity, non-foxy flavor.
varieties.description: Large conical clusters of yellow-green, non-slipskin seedless berries with moderately thick, crack-resistant skin and a fruity flavor without foxiness. Ripens in September; One Green World lists zones 6-9, hardy to -10F.

varieties.name: Interlaken
varieties.summary: Very early seedless green-gold table grape with crunchy non-slip berries.
varieties.description: Small to medium crunchy, green-to-golden, non-slipskin seedless berries with a robust American flavor, for fresh eating and raisins. Ripens very early (early September), suiting cool-summer areas. Raintree rates it cold hardy to zone 6.

varieties.name: Glenora
varieties.summary: Seedless blue-black table grape with mild, pleasant flavor.
varieties.description: Medium-sized blue-black seedless berries with a mild sweet flavor, good for fresh eating; ripens late August to early September. Roots to Fruits rates it zones 5-9 and notes phylloxera resistance.

varieties.name: Lakemont
varieties.summary: Seedless white table grape, a Himrod sibling with milder flavor.
varieties.description: Compact clusters of fairly small, mild-flavored seedless green berries. Double A describes it as a sibling of Himrod with reduced cold tolerance, so it may need a sheltered site in zone 6.

varieties.name: Valiant
varieties.summary: Extremely hardy blue grape for jelly, juice and fresh eating, zones 3-8.
varieties.description: Small compact clusters of small blue berries that ripen reliably in short, cold seasons; used for fresh eating, jam, jelly, juice and wine with a tangy flavor. Ripens late August; self-fertile, rated zones 3-8 and hardy to -50F at One Green World.

varieties.name: Compassion
varieties.summary: Seedless light-green grape from the University of Arkansas program.
varieties.description: Large clusters of firm, thick-skinned light green berries with above-average sweetness, for fresh eating and juice; some berries may carry faint seed remnants. Late bud break gives frost protection; Fedco rates it zone 5 and cites full crops in Vermont after -13F.

breeder.name: University of Arkansas grape breeding program (introduced 2017)

varieties.name: Fredonia
varieties.summary: Early Concord-type blue grape ripening about two weeks ahead of Concord.
varieties.description: Blue-black berries of Concord type used as a table grape and for processing and wine; ripens late August to early September, about two weeks before Concord. Roots to Fruits rates it zones 4-8.

varieties.name: Marquette
varieties.summary: University of Minnesota cold-hardy red wine grape with Pinot Noir-style character.
varieties.description: Small to medium clusters of bluish-black berries with high sugar, lower acidity than Frontenac and notable tannins, making complex ruby wines with cherry, berry and pepper notes. Fedco rates it zone 3 and reports fruit after -36F; early budbreak calls for good frost drainage.

varieties.name: Frontenac
varieties.summary: Very cold-hardy University of Minnesota red wine grape with cherry aromas.
varieties.description: Very large loose clusters of small ruby-dark berries with high sugar and high acidity, used for dry red, rose, port and sweet wines. Roots to Fruits reports hardiness to -35F and downy mildew immunity; Fedco advises waiting until late September to harvest.

varieties.name: La Crescent
varieties.summary: Cold-hardy white wine grape with apricot and citrus notes, from the University of Minnesota.
varieties.description: High-acid, Muscat-influenced berries producing off-dry to sweet wines with apricot, peach and citrus character, suited to dessert and late-harvest styles. Roots to Fruits reports hardiness to -36F (zones 4-9) with a late-September harvest.

varieties.name: Brianna
varieties.summary: Cold-hardy golden grape with pineapple and grapefruit flavors, for wine or fresh eating.
varieties.description: Medium-large thick-skinned gold berries with pineapple, grapefruit and floral flavors, used for semi-sweet wine and fresh eating. Late bud break and good secondary-bud fruiting help it handle cold; Roots to Fruits reports hardiness to -30F and good disease resistance.

varieties.name: Itasca
varieties.summary: University of Minnesota white wine grape with low acid and high sugar.
varieties.description: Golden-yellow berries with low acid and high sugar that make a dry Sauvignon Blanc-style wine, and also usable for fresh eating and juice. Fedco notes early budbreak, vigorous upright growth, disease resistance and survival of -38F.

varieties.name: Sabrevois
varieties.summary: Very hardy, disease-resistant dark red wine grape used for blending.
varieties.description: Small to medium clusters of nearly black fruit with moderate sugar and slightly high acidity, making a dry, aromatic red wine that blends well with higher-sugar reds like Frontenac. Vigorous and upright; Fedco rates it hardy to about -30F (zone 4).

varieties.name: Maréchal Foch
varieties.summary: Early French-American hybrid red wine grape, hardy to about -22F.
varieties.description: Small loose clusters of small black-red berries with blackberry, cherry and earthy notes for Burgundy-style wines, port and rose. Early ripening; Fedco says it is hardy to about -22F but breaks bud early, so site selection matters.

varieties.name: St. Pepin
varieties.summary: Cold-hardy white wine grape; female-flowered, needs a pollinating grape nearby.
varieties.description: Rather loose clusters of firm, medium greenish-white aromatic berries for white wine and juice without a musky flavor; also eaten fresh. Fedco rates it zone 4. The vine has female flowers and needs another variety blooming at the same time for fruit set.

varieties.name: L'Acadie Blanc
varieties.summary: Hardy Nova Scotian white wine grape with crisp apple and pear notes.
varieties.description: Early-season loose clusters of golden-green fruit that make crisp, mineral wines with apple and pear notes, single-varietal, blended or sparkling. Fedco rates it zone 4 (hardy to -20F or colder), and one grower reports it came through the Feb 2023 deep freeze.

breeder.name: Ollie A. Bradt, Vineland Station, Ontario (1953)

varieties.name: Adalmiina
varieties.summary: Hardy Swenson white wine grape from Concord x riparia, light and floral.
varieties.description: Golden-green grapes in medium loose clusters with low Brix (19-20) and low acidity, making a light floral, citrusy dry white wine with mineral pineapple notes. Fedco rates it zone 4 (about -30F) and describes it as still fairly obscure.

varieties.name: Louise Swenson
varieties.summary: Very hardy yellow-gold white wine grape with floral, honey and tangerine aromas.
varieties.description: Modest clusters of medium yellow-gold berries, naturally low in sugar with moderate acidity, making a light-bodied dry white wine with floral and honey aromas. Roots to Fruits reports hardiness to -40F (zones 3-9) and modest yields.

varieties.name: Prairie Star
varieties.summary: Very hardy Swenson-selected white wine grape with neutral aromatics.
varieties.description: Long, loose clusters on a vigorous vine producing a low-acid white wine without foxiness, often used for blending. Roots to Fruits reports hardiness to -38F (zones 3-9); Double A notes inconsistent fruit set in some seasons.

varieties.name: Swenson Red
varieties.summary: Large red non-slipskin grape, listed for table and white-style wine use.
varieties.description: Medium to large conical clusters of large, round, non-slipskin berries with firm flesh. Double A recommends it for white-style winemaking without skin fermentation, and One Green World sells it as a table grape. Hardiness is not stated on the pages read.

varieties.name: St. Croix
varieties.summary: Cold-hardy red wine grape giving light to medium burgundy-style wine.
varieties.description: Makes wine compared to a light to medium burgundy, with low sugar and minimal tannin, bottled alone or blended. Double A lists NYS-certified own-rooted stock; hardiness is not stated on the page read.

varieties.name: Edelweiss
varieties.summary: White labrusca-type grape bred as a table grape, also made into sweet wine.
varieties.description: Medium berries on large loose clusters; wine tends toward sweetness with pineapple or tropical notes, picked at 14-16 Brix to limit labrusca character. Hardiness is not stated on the pages read.

varieties.name: Delaware
varieties.summary: Early red table grape with small berries and fruity, mild flavor.
varieties.description: Early ripening small red berries with mild fruity flavor and little labrusca character, used fresh and for dry, sweet, ice and sparkling wine. Needs deep, fertile, well-drained soil and good fruit-zone exposure. Hardiness is not stated on the page read.

varieties.name: Steuben
varieties.summary: Spicy slipskin blue grape for aromatic white, blush or rose wine.
varieties.description: Large compact clusters of medium spherical slipskin berries with a spicy tang, used for aromatic white, blush and rose wine. Double A lists NYS-certified own-rooted stock; hardiness is not stated on the page read.

varieties.name: Beta
varieties.summary: Small blue-black American-type grape for juice and jelly, among the hardiest of its kind.
varieties.description: A small-berried, blue-black American-type grape used for juice, jelly and wine, grown for its extreme winter hardiness. Ripens early to mid season with a tart, strongly flavored fruit. Generally vigorous and disease tolerant.
notes: Seen sold out at Roots to Fruits Oct 7, 2026.

varieties.name: Traminette
varieties.summary: Gewurztraminer-type hybrid white wine grape with better winter hardiness than its parent.
varieties.description: A Gewurztraminer hybrid making distinctive, spicy wines that can be finished dry or semi-dry. Double A describes it as much more winter hardy than Gewurztraminer.

varieties.name: Vidal Blanc
varieties.summary: Productive white hybrid wine grape suited to late harvest and ice wine.
varieties.description: Medium berries on very large, compact clusters; thick skins with strong rot resistance. Makes semi-dry wine or blends with other white hybrids, and suits late-harvest and ice wine styles.

varieties.name: Petite Pearl
varieties.summary: Cold-hardy blue-black red wine grape from Minnesota breeder Tom Plocher.
varieties.description: Small to medium clusters of deep blue-black, high-tannin fruit make full-bodied red wine. Vines are productive with good disease resistance and spread 15-20 ft or more on a trellis. Edible Landscaping rates it zones 4-8.

varieties.name: Verona
varieties.summary: Late-budding, cold-hardy red wine grape bred by Tom Plocher.
varieties.description: Large clusters of blue-black grapes for premium red wine, from a 1997 cross. Moderately vigorous and productive, with late spring bud break that helps avoid frost damage. Edible Landscaping rates it zones 4-8; needs a trellis.

varieties.name: Veritage
varieties.summary: Cold-hardy red wine grape bred by Tom Plocher for frost resistance.
varieties.description: Large clusters of dark blue-black grapes make deeply colored red wine with raspberry, plum and black-pepper notes. Vines reach 15-20 ft or more and need a trellis. Edible Landscaping rates it zones 4-8.

varieties.name: Thomcord
varieties.summary: Seedless Concord x Thompson Seedless cross with sweet Concord-style flavor.
varieties.description: Blue-black seedless berries with sweet Concord-style flavor ripen in August. Self-pollinating and heat tolerant, growing 4-6 ft with 6-8 ft spacing per Stark Bro's, which rates it zones 5-9.

varieties.name: Saint Theresa
varieties.summary: Cold-hardy purple grape, mostly seedless, reported to survive -30F.
varieties.description: Sweet, juicy mostly seedless purple fruit ripens in early September. Self-pollinating, tolerates alkaline soil and partial shade; Stark Bro's rates it zones 4-9 and reports survival to -30F.

varieties.name: King of the North
varieties.summary: Seeded blue grape rated hardy to zone 3.
varieties.description: Seeded blue Vitis labrusca-type grape listed by Berry Plants for zones 3-7, among the hardiest of the American table types on file.

varieties.name: Corot Noir
varieties.summary: Cornell red wine hybrid with cherry and berry notes, rated for zones 5-8.
varieties.description: A Cornell hybrid (Seyve Villard 18-307 x Steuben) released in 2006 for deep red wines with berry and cherry aromas, used alone or in blends. Vigorous, semi-upright vine with bud break 5-7 days after Concord and a late-season harvest. Double A rates it for USDA zones 5-8.

varieties.name: Noiret
varieties.summary: Cornell red wine hybrid with peppery, Syrah-like character.
varieties.description: A Cornell red wine grape released in 2006 (NY65.0467.08 x Steuben) making full-bodied, richly colored wine with black pepper, raspberry, blackberry and mint notes. Vines are vigorous with typically low yields and a late harvest. Double A lists it for USDA zones 5-12.

varieties.name: Cayuga White
varieties.summary: Productive, disease-resistant Cornell white wine hybrid for semi-dry to sweet wine.
varieties.description: Cornell's first variety released specifically for winemaking (1972, Seyval x Schuyler), making semi-dry to sweet white wine often blended with Seyval and Vidal. Self-fertile, vigorous, semi-trailing vine ripening mid-season, described as one of the most productive and disease-resistant grapes in New York. Double A rates it for zones 5-8.
